title: How to settle a group trip in 4 payments, not 16
description:
Five friends, four people paid for something: that's 16 IOUs if everyone pays back every receipt. Instead, add it all up (800 dollars, 160 each) and work out each person's balance: paid minus share. Then the biggest debt pays the biggest credit, again and again. Every payment brings at least one person to zero, so five people never need more than 4 payments, and here 4 is the minimum because no smaller group balances on its own. Splitwise's "simplify debts" setting does the same kind of restructuring.

Numbers checked in code: the balances, the four payments, that no subgroup sums to zero, and 100,000 random groups of 2 to 10 people (the greedy settle-up never needed more than n-1 payments). Source: Splitwise help, kb.splitwise.com/balances-and-expenses/what-is-simplify-debts.

beats.say: Pay every debt: 16 transfers. Settle the totals: 4.
Nobody pays a cent more or less. You just stop paying back receipts.
Five friends. You paid the 400 dollar hotel, Ana the car, Tom the dinners, Max the fuel.
Step 1: forget the receipts. 800 dollars total, so 160 each.
Step 2: paid minus share. You're up 240, Tom's up 40. Ana's down 10, Max 110, Zoe 160.
Now the trick: who pays whom doesn't matter. Every balance just has to hit zero.
Step 3: the biggest debt pays the biggest credit. Zoe sends you 160. Done.
Repeat. Max sends you 80, and Tom 30. Ana sends Tom 10. Everyone's at zero.
Each payment clears at least one person, so five friends never need more than 4.
Three friends: you're up 50, Ana's down 20, Tom's down 30. How many payments?
